engine: Silencio-2 (BlueRoseLabs) - emotion-tag fine-tune of Pocket TTS 18M
latest_version: Silencio-2, HF repo created 2026-10-31, last modified 2026-11-01 (4 commits). No GitHub repo, no PyPI package.
code_license: MIT (silencio2/core is Kyutai Pocket TTS inference code, MIT)
weights_license: cc-by-4.0 (HF license tag); fine-tune of kyutai/pocket-tts, also CC-BY-4.0
commercial_notes: CC-BY-4.0 permits commercial use with attribution: credit Silencio-2/BlueRoseLabs and Kyutai Pocket TTS (e.g. in video description or app credits). NOTICE.md says it was developed using the Basis Global Emotions dataset; I did not check that dataset's licence.
params: 27.9M total (18.2M speech generation + Mimi encoder for cloning). English only, 24 kHz.
vram_gb_min: Not stated; trivially small. CPU is the intended target.
speed_note: Model card: 'about 20x faster than real time on four CPU threads of an Apple M4' (RTF ~0.05). quantize=True loads int8 on CPU. No x86 figure.
windows_install: `hf download BlueRoseLabs/Silencio-2 --local-dir Silencio-2`, then inside that folder `uv pip install -r requirements.txt` (torch>=2.5, numpy>=2, pydantic>=2, pyyaml, sentencepiece>=0.2.1, tokenizers>=0.21, safetensors, scipy, einops, huggingface_hub, requests, typing_extensions, soundfile). Import `silencio2` from the cloned folder (it is not a pip package). No Windows statement; every dependency has Windows wheels and nothing needs a compiler.
instruct_on_cloned_voice: Partial, not free text. Fixed emotion tags <happy> <sad> <angry> <fear> <surprised> <whisper> (or emotion= kwarg) and sound tags [laugh] [sigh] [gasp] [cough] [clear_throat]; cloning is voice="my_clip.wav". The API lets you pass both, but the card does not say explicitly that emotion tags hold up on a cloned voice.
emotion_controls: 6 emotion tags, 5 sound tags; unknown tags raise an error; <whisper> is the least consistent.
speed_control: None. seed= supported ('trying several seeds may help').
minimal_python_usage:
from silencio2 import Silencio2TTS

tts = Silencio2TTS.from_pretrained()  # add quantize=True for int8 on CPU
tts.save("clone.wav", "Hi! This is my voice.", voice="my_clip.wav")
wav = tts.generate("...", seed=7)  # 1-D float32 tensor
cloning_quality_note: No evaluation of any kind on the card (no WER, SIM or MOS) and no independent reports: 351 downloads and 22 likes after 12 days. Quality ceiling is that of an 18M Pocket-TTS-class model, i.e. below the 100M+ engines; cloning is described only as working 'from a few seconds of reference audio'.
known_issues: Delivery varies between takes; important lines 'should be checked by ear'; English only; tiny community, single upload, could disappear or change.
verdict_reason: Costs 116 MB and a few minutes: commercial-OK with attribution, 20x realtime on CPU, no transcript, and the only tiny model here with emotion tags plus a seed. But it is a 12-day-old hobby-scale fine-tune of Pocket TTS (already on your list) with zero published evaluation, so treat it as an optional add-on to the Pocket TTS test rather than a primary candidate.

latest_version: pocket-tts 4.0.1 on PyPI (2026-10-21). Default English checkpoint = english_2026-10 (219 MB, float32); HF repo kyutai/pocket-tts last updated 2026-10-21. Oct 2026 also added tiny English models (18.2M / 6.9M / 1.9M params) and a preview 24-layer English model (english_2026-09_24l, 1.3 GB).
weights_license: CC-BY-4.0 (HF tag 'cc-by-4.0' on kyutai/pocket-tts). The cloning-capable repo is gated (gated=auto): accept terms + HF login.
commercial_notes: CC BY 4.0 permits commercial use with attribution (credit 'Pocket TTS by Kyutai, CC BY 4.0' in the description to be safe). Model card 'Prohibited use' bans cloning a voice without explicit lawful consent, so clone only your own / a consenting speaker. The bundled catalog voices have their own per-voice licences (irrelevant if you clone your own clip).
vram_gb_min: 0 (designed for CPU). Optional unofficial GPU use via tts_model.to('cuda'); ~100M fp32 params, well under 1 GB.
speed_note: Official README: ~6x realtime on MacBook Air M4 using 2 CPU cores, ~200 ms to first audio; 2.3-2.5x realtime on a 4-vCPU cloud x86 VM (6.28x on a Tesla T4). No Ryzen 5 5600H figure published; expect roughly 2-4x realtime (my extrapolation, unmeasured). All weights float32, so the GTX 16xx fp16 problem does not apply.
download_size_gb: ~0.22 (model.safetensors 219 MB + tokenizer); CPU-only torch wheel ~0.2 GB download on Windows
windows_install: uv venv --python 3.11; uv pip install pocket-tts soundfile  (needs torch>=2.5; on Windows the default PyPI torch wheel is already CPU-only, no extra index). For voice cloning: accept terms at https://huggingface.co/kyutai/pocket-tts then run `uvx hf auth login` (source code error message says exactly this; without it the library silently falls back to the no-cloning weights and only preset voices work). No espeak/pynini/triton. Alternative: prebuilt Windows x86 standalone binary (Rust port, CPU only) from GitHub releases. Avoid the optional [quantize] extra (torchao needs torch>=2.11).
instruct_on_cloned_voice: No. There is no style/instruction prompt and no emotion control; prosody follows the reference clip and the text.
emotion_controls: None. Sampling temperature only (load_model(temp=...), default 0.3), sampler_decode_steps (default 1), noise_clamp, eos_threshold, frames_after_eos. No documented seed parameter.
speed_control: None documented (no speed/rate parameter; no pause insertion - issue #6).
minimal_python_usage:
from pocket_tts import TTSModel
import scipy.io.wavfile
tts_model = TTSModel.load_model()
voice_state = tts_model.get_state_for_audio_prompt("./my_voice.wav")  # or truncate=True to cap at 30 s
audio = tts_model.generate_audio(voice_state, "Hello world, this is a test.")
scipy.io.wavfile.write("output.wav", tts_model.sample_rate, audio.numpy())
# cache the voice: from pocket_tts import export_model_state; export_model_state(voice_state, "my_voice.safetensors")
cloning_quality_note: No arena data: TTS Arena V2 API (fetched today, 45 models) does not list Pocket TTS. Independent review (andrew.ooo) relays an r/LocalLLaMA subjective comparison ranking cloning quality Pocket TTS > Supertonic > Inflect-Nano > Kokoro-forks, and says Kokoro still wins on fixed-voice quality and CPU speed. GitHub issue #115 (14 comments): users find prosody/tone below Kokoro's best voice and report occasional glitches on some words; #347 (open, Oct 2026) repeated phrase at sentence end; #221 inserted/repeated words. Reverb/noise in the reference is reproduced by design, so denoise the clip first. Kyutai's own report (secondhand via AlphaSignal) claims lowest WER in its class and speaker similarity comparable to F5-TTS. Output is 24 kHz.
known_issues: Cloning weights gated on HF. 24 kHz output. One Windows report (#189) of garbled cloning from a 24 kHz reference WAV, fixed by resampling the reference to 16 kHz (single user report). Occasional word repetition (#347, #221). No speed/emotion/pause control. GPU not officially supported.
verdict_reason: Best fit for this machine in this group: commercial-usable weights (CC BY 4.0), pure `pip install` on Windows, runs faster than realtime on CPU in float32 so the 1.4 GB-free GTX 1650 is irrelevant, no reference transcript, handles long text itself, ~0.2 GB. Weak points to A/B: similarity/prosody ceiling of a 100M model, 24 kHz, no style control.
